items.summary: DUBAI, Nov 23 (Reuters) - Iran will use all available tools to confront the US naval blockade, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said in a weekly news conference on Monday. The blockade on Iran-related oil exports was imposed on April 13, lifted in June after Washington reached a draft understanding with Tehran, then restored on July 14 after the agreement collapsed. items.summary: Iran launches attacks on military base in Kuwait Submitted by MEE staff on Wed, 11/18/2026 - 09:34 The Iranian army said it had targeted the Ali al-Salem Airbase in Kuwait, while the cause of a building fire in Bahrain is being investigated Missiles are put on display in central Tehran on 28 September (AFP) Off Iran has launched a series of attacks against its Gulf neighbours in Kuwait and Bahrain , as tensions continue to simmer. In a statement published on state media early on Wednesday, the Iranian army said it fired a drone targeting the Ali al-Salem Airbase in Kuwait. "This morning, the Islamic Republic of Iran's army's destructive combat drones targeted Patriot defense systems and drone and missile launchers of the US terrorist army at the Ali al-Salem base in Kuwait with destructive drones," the statement read. "In defense of Iran, we will not bow to any power, but our response to any threat or aggression will be decisive, crushing, and without geographical limitations," the army added Earlier, the Kuwaiti ⁠⁠military said ⁠⁠that its air defences were ⁠⁠countering the ⁠⁠attack.

items.title: Kuwait slams Iranian attacks on its territory
items.summary: Kuwait slams Iranian attacks on its territory Kuwait’s foreign ministry has condemned the latest Iranian drone attack on its territory. The ministry denounced the attacks as "repeated and criminal" and described it as a "direct threat" to the Gulf country's "security and stability". "The Ministry reaffirms that the continuation of these attacks constitutes a dangerous escalation that threatens the region’s security and stability and undermines diplomatic efforts aimed at de-escalation and reducing tensions," the ministry said in its statement posted on X. It added that Kuwait retains the right to "take all necessary measures to safeguard its sovereignty, preserve its security and defend its territory and vital facilities against any aggression or threat, in exercise of its inherent right to self-defence".

items.title: Iran's navy says three tankers on fire after hitting mines in Hormuz
items.summary: Nov 14 (Reuters) - Iran's navy said three oil tankers caught fire on Saturday after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported. One tanker hit a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz on Saturday morning, while two others struck mines later in the day. "Two violating tankers ... were attempting to slip through a prohibited route in the Strait of Hormuz when they hit naval mines, exploded, and burst into flames," Iran's IRNA news agency quoted the Revolutionary Guards Navy as saying about the evening incident.

items.title: Iran’s IRGC says two oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Iran’s IRGC says two oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz Two oil tankers struck naval mines as they tried to cross the Strait of Hormuz “secretly”, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy says. In a statement published by Iran’s state news agency IRNA, the navy said the ships switched off their tracking and navigation equipment and took an “unauthorised” route. “Following the explosions of these two tankers, two other tankers that were attempting to transit secretly complied with the warnings from the Naval Force’s traffic control centre in the Strait of Hormuz and returned towards the waters of the Persian Gulf,” the IRGC said.

The navy did not identify the vessel. It was the fifth oil tanker in 24 hours to catch fire after reportedly being struck by Iranian forces or hitting a naval mine while attempting to transit the strait.

items.title: China issues 'peace declaration' agreed with Trump and Putin
items.summary: China issues 'peace declaration' agreed with Trump and Putin China has released a “peace declaration” it said its President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin had agreed on at their unprecedented three-way meeting, where they said nuclear wars were futile and should never be fought. All three countries committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security, according to a four-point declaration published by Chinese official media Xinhua. The leaders reportedly discussed Russia's war in Ukraine and the US-Israeli war on Iran. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons, Xinhua said. The three heads of state also agreed on reform for a "more effective" United Nations, and said that the International Criminal Court and similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction, according to the declaration.

items.summary: Trump lands in China for meeting with Xi and Putin US President Donald Trump has arrived in China for the Apec summit in Shenzhen, where he is expected to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladmir Putin. The historic trilateral meeting between the leaders will take place on Thursday. Xi, Trump and Putin are due to meet on the sidelines of the summit to potentially discuss Russia's war with Ukraine and the US-Israeli war on Iran, as well as trade, AI and nuclear weapons. Xi met Trump off the plane on the tarmac at Shenzhen, reciprocating Trump's gesture when the Chinese leader visited the US in September. Xi told Trump he hoped their talks would help advance a “constructive, strategic and stable relationship” between China and the US, based on “respect, fairness and reciprocity”, according to China’s state news agency Xinhua. As the trial was running its course, Iranian drones were targeting U.S. military installations in Bahrain, with attacks taking place on Friday, Sunday, and again on Tuesday and Wednesday, ending a two-month lull. Bahrain, the small island kingdom on the eastern side of the Arabian Peninsula, is where the pressures of the U.S.-Iran war are concentrated most tightly. It signed the Abraham Accords with Israel, and is also a deeply indebted nation, dependent on its wealthier neighbors for its survival. items.title: The best thing I ever ate? Lunch on the strait of Hormuz
items.summary: The idea of any guest being hungry, or there not being enough food, is an unspeakable proposition for an Iranian host When most people think of the strait of Hormuz, the warm, tropical waterway connecting the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman, incredible food isn’t usually the first thing that comes to mind. But it should be, and I would know – it’s where I had one of my most memorable meals. I was visiting Iran, traversing thousands of miles across the country with a local female photographer, mapping out regional specialities for my cookbook The Saffron Tales . Over the course of several months, we cooked and ate in people’s home kitchens, meeting a cross-section of society, from farmers and pharmacists to yoga teachers and restaurant owners, who all shared their favourite foods with us in places as diverse as the snowy mountains outside Tabriz, the rice paddies of the Caspian Sea, and the historic cities of Isfahan and Shiraz. In its weekly report published on Friday, UKMTO said four of the six incidents occurred in the Strait of Hormuz and two in the Arabian Gulf. The UKMTO recorded 115 outbound and 148 inbound transits during the seven days to November 18, including US-facilitated movements. The combined figure was down from 139 outbound and 169 inbound the previous week. Around half of Strait of Hormuz transits involved energy carriers. Most vessels broadcasting AIS continued to use the Iranian route, although UKMTO noted an increase in traffic along the southern route. No attacks were recorded in the past week in the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandab, with the last confirmed attack recorded on August 24. The meeting came as Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani was in Germany on a visit. Following talks with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Berlin, the emir called for diplomatic efforts to de-escalate conflicts across the Middle East. On the sidelines of the visit, Qatari Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani met his German counterpart Johann Wadephul. items.summary: Trump says US will find out about Iranian dirty bomb plot 'rumour' US President Donald Trump said on Friday that there was a "rumour" that Iran was building a dirty bomb. He added that if Iran was doing so, the United States would find out and stop it. CNN had reported earlier this week that US intelligence indicated Iran could be attempting to build a dirty bomb and detonate it in Washington. Iran's foreign ministry denied the allegations on Tuesday, calling them "baseless". A dirty bomb is far less destructive than a nuclear bomb, which relies on a fission reaction. Speaking to reporters, Trump also repeated his claim that the US has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz. "Last week, we took out record amounts of oil from the Hormuz Strait. Our navy has a blockade," he said. "We have total control over the Hormuz Strait." "Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, ever," he added. items.title: What Ukraine Hath Wrought: Lessons for War, If We’re Listening
items.summary: Four years into Russia’s war against Ukraine, what should the U.S. military have learned by now? Michael Kofman (Carnegie Endowment), Dara Massicot (Carnegie Endowment), and Amos Fox (Arizona State University) join Ryan to discuss. The easy answer is drones and AI, but our guests argue the harder truths lie elsewhere: “Old-fashioned” ideas like campaigning, holding territory, mass, and attrition still decide wars. And, as they discuss, based on U.S. performance in the war with Iran, it may be that not much learning has happened at all.Image: ArmyInform The post What Ukraine Hath Wrought: Lessons for War, If We’re Listening appeared first on War on the Rocks .

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said shortly afterwards that an oil tanker had caught fire after hitting a mine while attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz near Khasab, Iranian media reported. Khasab is located on Oman's Musandam Peninsula at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz.

items.summary: US must leave West Asia and return to its own region, Iranian lawmaker says An Iranian lawmaker said the United States must withdraw from West Asia and return to its own geographic sphere. Major-General Mohammad Esmaeil Kowsari, a member of parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, told Iran’s Mehr news agency that the US could no longer confront Iran. He said Washington had issued shifting threats, at times discussing military action on the ground and at others threatening to open the Strait of Hormuz. Kowsari also pointed to US threats against Iran’s nuclear programme and proposals for an economic, land, air and naval blockade of the country. He said that Washington should leave West Asia and return to its own geographical sphere, which he said was 12,000km away.

clusters.headline: Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper hit in Houthi strike on Saudi wealth fund HQ

items.title: Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper hit in Houthi strike on Saudi wealth fund HQ
items.summary: By Timour Azhari RIYADH, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Riyadh's tallest skyscraper, headquarters of the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, was struck on Thursday by a suspected Houthi missile in the latest blow in the Iran-backed Yemeni group's war with the kingdom. The strike blew out windows across seven to eight floors of PIF Tower, bending parts of its metal facade. It was the second time in less than two weeks that a Houthi attack damaged a landmark in Riyadh's financial district, with state oil giant Aramco's building hit in a November 8 attack.

items.summary: De energiecrisis die is veroorzaakt door de oorlog tussen de VS en Iran, zal blijvende sporen achterlaten op de energiemarkt. Dat zegt het internationaal energie-agentschap IEA in zijn jaarlijkse rapport over de energiemarkt. Door de oorlog konden er een deel van dit jaar geen olietankers meer door de Straat van Hormuz tussen Iran en Oman, terwijl juist door die zeestraat een groot deel van de olie uit het Midden-Oosten naar de rest van de wereld wordt geëxporteerd. Gigantische klap De afsluiting leidde tot torenhoge benzine- diesel- en kerosineprijzen. "De Hormuz-crisis gaf het energiesysteem een gigantische klap", zegt IEA-directeur Fatih Birol. "De energiesector en de wereldeconomie hebben dan wel weerbaarheid laten zien. Maar hoe langer de crisis duurt, hoe dieper deze zijn sporen nalaat. Ik zie geen geloofwaardige manier waarop de energiewereld teruggaat naar hoe het hiervoor was." Het agentschap doet niet één toekomstvoorspelling, maar schetst verschillende scenario's van hoe de energiewereld zich zal ontwikkelen. It is a historic moment in more ways than one, with the leaders of the world’s three most powerful countries around the same table. Ukraine, the war in Iran, nuclear disarmament and artificial intelligence are all expected to be discussed, and the summit has stoked fears of a carve-up of the world into spheres of influence. But despite the buzz, analysts expect more symbolism than substance, with few concrete breakthroughs likely. Our correspondent in the region has more.

items.summary: Iran's navy says three oil tankers caught fire east of Hormuz The Iranian navy said on Wednesday that three oil tankers caught fire and were disabled after hitting naval mines while sailing east of the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's Press TV. In a statement carried by the IRIB news agency, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said the tankers had ignored warnings from its naval forces as they navigated in restricted areas with navigation systems disabled and passage through the waterway must be coordinated with Iranian authorities.

items.summary: Iran's IRGC says two tankers ablaze in Hormuz The IRGC reports that two tankers caught fire after colliding with naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. In comments carried by Iran's Fars News Agency, the IRGC's navy said that one of the ships was a supertanker carrying over 2m barrels of crude oil, while the other was transporting liquefied natural gas. It added that both vessels, which it said were supported by US forces, had breached Iran's protocol for crossing the contested waterway.

In this way, even if the meeting — which is supposed to take place Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit — leads to no concrete results, it will still be worth doing. items.title: Rubio says 'no imminent threat' to US from Iran
items.summary: Rubio says 'no imminent threat' to US from Iran US Secretary of State Marco Rubio cast doubt about reports of an "imminent threat" from Iran on Washington. Speaking to reporters in the Philippines, Rubio said that US authorities routinely check for  potential threats against the country, but added that most intelligence leads are not considered credible. When asked if he was concerned about a possible attack on Washington, he said: "I am not. But again, we're concerned every day about anything that threatens our country ... I don't think there's any imminent threat. "The United States is always on the lookout for anyone who tries to do harm to our country and to our people. And we have threat streams every day, and the majority of them are not credible. We have to follow up on them," Rubio added. Rubio also questioned the credibility of sources cited in a CNN report about an alleged Iranian plot targeting the US capital, saying: "Some of your intelligence sources are liars; others are liars and criminals." items.summary: Taxpayer money is flowing to the Pentagon at record levels, yet the Pentagon can’t actually tell you where all that money is going. That’s the conclusion from the Pentagon’s 9th consecutive failed financial audit , which continues to leave the Pentagon as the only major federal Department to have never received a “clean” department-wide audit. items.title: Iran-backed Iraqi group refuses to withdraw from stronghold
items.summary: Iran-backed Iraqi group refuses to withdraw from stronghold Kataeb Hezbollah, Iraq's Iran-backed paramilitary group, said it will not leave its stronghold despite the US-backed prime minister calling on the armed faction to withdraw and allow the army to enter. On Monday, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi gave Kataeb Hezbollah an unspecified deadline to withdraw from Jurf al-Sakher, south of Baghdad, after the government earlier said an investigative committee had confirmed oil smuggling in the area - a claim the armed group denied. "I can state decisively and with absolute certainty that the dream they dream of the Kataeb withdrawing from Jurf al-Sakher will not come true, not even over our dead bodies," Abu Taleb al-Saidi, a Kataeb Hezbollah commander, told AFP during a press visit to the area. A security source told AFP that the deadline for Kataeb Hezbollah to withdraw from the area south of Baghdad was on Friday. Saidi stressed that his group did not want a confrontation with Iraqi armed forces.

items.title: Giacca, cravatta e 20 flessioni: perché l'ambasciatore Waltz fa piegamenti con i Marines a Beirut
items.summary: In giacca e cravatta, si mette a terra insieme a un gruppo di Marines e comincia a fare piegamenti sulle braccia. È il gesto con cui Mike Waltz, ambasciatore degli Stati Uniti all'Onu, ha voluto ricordare i 241 militari americani uccisi nell'attentato alla caserma dei Marines di Beirut, in Libano, il 23 ottobre 1983. Nel video, pubblicato su X il 17 novembre, Waltz esegue 20 flessioni insieme ai militari impegnati nella sicurezza dell'ambasciata statunitense nella capitale libanese. Le immagini sono accompagnate da un messaggio dedicato alle vittime dell'attacco, che gli Stati Uniti attribuiscono a Hezbollah e all'Iran.L'attentato del 1983, avvenuto durante la guerra civile libanese, provocò la morte di 220 Marines, 18 marinai della Marina e tre soldati dell'Esercito americano.

An internet blackout imposed at the time of the crackdown on January 8 and 9 and the scale of the casualties meant it was not yet possible for the group to quantify the number of people killed, Amnesty's lead Iran researcher, Raha Bahreini, said.

New rule: Any dam, port, or power plant near a US or Israeli base is dual-use. We’ll apply your logic consistently and even-handedly," Ghalibaf added. The US and Israel have previously attacked civilian areas and infrastructure across the region under the guise that they are used for military purpose, despite having no evidence for such claims. items.summary: Syria appears likely to soon join the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, a collective defense agreement established several months ago by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan. This development would constitute a milestone in Damascus’ efforts to reassert itself within the region’s security architecture following Syria’s gruesome civil war. Membership in the pact could enhance the legitimacy and prestige of post-Assad Syria while bolstering its military capabilities and deepening partnerships with influential regional states. Syria could benefit from more intelligence cooperation, military training, and Saudi financial support. All this could complement Damascus’ existing security partnership with Ankara. But it’s not all milk and honey. Joining the security configuration could expose Syria to foreign conflicts and geopolitical rivalries while undermining Damascus’ ability to prioritize redevelopment at home. Woorden van die strekking liepen drie jaar geleden nog uit op een felle strijd, maar voorzitter Australië probeert het nu toch weer. Tot tweemaal toe wordt er expliciet naar fossiele brandstoffen gewezen in de slottekst van de klimaattop, waar het tot nu toe vrijwel ieder jaar extreem ingewikkeld blijkt om teksten aangenomen te krijgen over dit thema. Landen hebben vanaf nu de kans om te reageren op de tekst, waarmee eind deze week de klimaattop wordt afgesloten. De passages zouden dus nog aangepast of geschrapt kunnen worden. Dat gebeurde drie jaar geleden nog op de klimaattop in Dubai, toen eveneens werd geprobeerd om de handen op elkaar te krijgen voor het "uitfaseren" van fossiele brandstoffen. items.summary: The Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) is staring down the barrel of entering 2027 without a chair for the first time in its 51-year history. The Europeans are wrestling Turkey to drop its veto over Cyprus’ bid, raising the stakes by loudly opposing the only other candidate, Georgia. Unable to win over Ankara, Europe should drop its objections to Tbilisi to avert a crisis. With three weeks to go until the OSCE Ministerial Council in Lugano, Switzerland, on December 3, the organization remains deadlocked over who should lead it from 2027-28. The chairperson-in-office role rotates every two years and is normally voted on well in advance with agreement by consensus. EU member Cyprus was the first country to put its hat in the ring almost two years ago, in December 2024. However, Cyprus’ bid has been vetoed by Turkey on the basis of the long-standing dispute over the division of the island in 1974 . items.title: Trump's Africa envoy puts on a masterclass in bad diplomacy
items.summary: Since returning to the White House, President Donald Trump has increasingly relied on special envoys to deal with some of his most vexing foreign policy challenges. While Trump slashed the use of special envoys in his first term, he has come around in his second term, in part because they allow him to bypass his career foreign service officers by compartmentalizing information from “deep state bureaucrats” who he has accused of spying on him and leaking his dealmaking to the press. As in previous administrations, the current Trump administration has assembled a collection of envoys largely based on region and policy imperative. Regions like the Middle East, South and Central Asia, and the Arctic all have special envoys, as do specific countries like Syria, Belarus, Greenland, and Ukraine (currently vacant). clusters.headline: A Second Path Under the Caspian: What the Trans-Caspian Cable Changes for Eurasian Connectivity

items.title: A Second Path Under the Caspian: What the Trans-Caspian Cable Changes for Eurasian Connectivity
items.summary: When the presidents of Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan inaugurated a 380-kilometer fiber-optic cable beneath the Caspian Sea on October 15, they opened the first fiber-optic link across the Caspian seabed. Designed for a capacity of at least 400 terabits per second, the cable matters chiefly because it creates an alternative: data moving between Central Asia and Europe can now take a westbound route that avoids Russian networks. Kazakhstan gains an additional international connection, and Azerbaijan strengthens its role as a transit hub. Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, which depend on Kazakhstan for international connectivity, stand to gain indirectly, and carriers and cloud providers gain another potential route between Asia and Europe. How far these gains extend will depend on how much traffic the link comes to carry.

items.title: En Auschwitz con el heredero del Sah de Irán para apoyar a los judíos
items.summary: En fila india, en silencio y tiritando de frío, nuestras sombras avanzan por un túnel oscuro camino del matadero. A través de ese pasaje subterráneo en el que suenan los nombres de los judíos que aquí fueron exterminados, la visita al campo de concentración de Auschwitz sobrecoge desde la entrada, incluso antes de llegar a la puerta de hierro con su infame cartel 'El trabajo os hará libre' ('ARBEIT MACHT FREI', escrito en alemán en mayúsculas). Cuentan que la B de 'ARBEIT' ('trabajo') está al revés, más ancha por arriba que por abajo, porque así la puso un herrero polaco preso en el campo, Jan Liwacz, como pequeño gesto de rebeldía para demostrar la falsedad del eslogan: aquí nada traía la libertad, solo la muerte.Se calcula que en el campo de Auschwitz y en el de Birkenau, a tres kilómetros y medio, perecieron un millón de los seis millones de judíos que los nazis mataron en el Holocausto durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial (1939-45). The IRGC accused Israel of spreading misinformation. French authorities blame Shahid Kaveh for what they describe as the first large-scale cyber sabotage on French soil. On October 11 and 12, hackers drove temperatures inside refrigeration units to as high as 50C (122F) at about 700 stores. “Paris should beware the Zionist regime’s false flag trap,” IRGC spokesman Sardar Mohebi said on X. “Unlike the US and the Zionist regime, civilians have no place on the target list of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps,” he said, adding that the “ridiculous claim” is the “Zionists’ tired old playbook for stoking fear of Iran and winning allies in Europe”.

items.summary: 'What would be left of international legal order': Araghchi on US strikes "If states were free to attack one another based on their own assessments of possible future threats, what would be left of the international legal order?" Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has asked in an opinion piece for Japan's Kyodo News. "This question," Araghchi wrote, "goes well beyond the political dispute between Iran and the United States." "It concerns one of the fundamental principles on which the international order established after the Second World War rests: the use of force is governed by law, and no state, however powerful, is entitled to place its own judgment above binding rules of international law," the article read. He said the US-Israeli strikes constituted a clear violation of the prohibition on the use of force and an infringement of Iran's sovereignty. "Their legality must be assessed against the U.N. Briefing the UN Security Council on Friday, Khiari cited figures from the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) covering incidents recorded up to November 11. He said October saw the highest monthly number of incidents involving commercial shipping since February, warning that continued disruption was driving up energy, transport and insurance costs and threatening global food security. “This situation cannot be allowed to become the new normal,” Khiari said, calling for an immediate end to attacks on civilian vessels and the restoration of safe maritime navigation. items.summary: US says it shot down two Iranian drones heading towards Bahrain The US military on Friday said it had shot down two Iranian attack drones launched towards Bahrain, denying an Iranian claim that its forces had struck a US early-warning radar system in the Gulf kingdom. US Central Command (Centcom) said the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launched two one-way attack drones towards Bahrain, both of which were intercepted by US forces. Centcom also rejected the IRGC’s claim that it had attacked a US early-warning radar in Bahrain earlier in the day. The competing accounts come amid questions from some US lawmakers about the Pentagon’s disclosure of details surrounding incidents in the conflict, while scepticism has also circulated on social media.

items.title: Trump extends shipping law waiver for 90 days amid Iran war fuel price rise
items.summary: Trump extends shipping law waiver for 90 days amid Iran war fuel price rise US President Donald Trump has extended by 90 days a waiver of a shipping law so that foreign-flagged ships can transport oil and other commodities between US ports, a White House official said on Friday. The administration would extend the waiver of the more than 100-year-old Jones Act, Reuters reported, citing industry sources. The administration issued a blanket waiver in March, a month after the US launched its war on Iran, in an effort to lower oil and fuel prices. When it extended the waiver in August, it said it would decide cases on a case-by-case basis, a condition that also applies to the latest extension. The Jones Act requires cargo moving between US ports to be carried on ships built in the US, owned by US companies, and crewed by American workers. The waiver aims to lower gasoline, diesel, and fertiliser prices, which have risen because of the war. items.title: Opinion: Anti-Muslim racism is a global system used to normalise mass killing
items.summary: Opinion: Anti-Muslim racism is a global system used to normalise mass killing Dr Amina Shareef, a researcher of anti-Muslim racism, says that the destruction unfolding in Gaza, Iran and Lebanon is part of a longer history of anti-Muslim racism that has made mass Muslim suffering and death politically permissible. She says that Islamophobia is not simply a matter of prejudice or discrimination, but a global system of racial power that constructs Muslims and those identified as Muslim as security threats, allowing violence against them to be justified in the name of security. Central to this system is the figure of the Muslim terrorist, which portrays Muslim political agency as inherently threatening. Shareef says that this logic extends beyond surveillance, detention and militarised borders to warfare, political abandonment and the destruction of the conditions necessary for life. "Wat we in november zagen was zeer interessant", zegt expert energiemarkt van Essent Dennie van Zon. "Onder normale temperaturen zagen we bij gasgebruik normaal gedrag, maar op 3 november, toen het 1 graad onder de normale temperatuur was, zagen we al tot 4 procent minder gasverbruik." Voornamelijk in de avonduren werd er meer elektrisch bijgestookt. "We zagen echt als mensen thuiskomen tussen 17.00 en 18.00 uur een toename van elektrisch bijstoken. items.summary: Sen. Thom Tillis (R–N.C.) has moved to prevent a fast-track confirmation of Alexander Alden, President Donald Trump’s nominee to be the next U.S. ambassador to Azerbaijan. Far from a bureaucratic hurdle, the move will likely force Alden, who has served in Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s office with the title of senior advisor since early 2025, to answer uncomfortable questions over possible conflicts of interests in his financial dealings, and, consequently, about his inclination to prioritize U.S. foreign policy in Baku. Alden has substantial financial interests in Palantir, the defense and intelligence technology company that currently has defense tech and intelligence contracts with the U.S. government worth billions of dollars . In fact, roughly half of its revenue stream comes from government clients globally. Each of these concerns would justify subjecting Alden’s nomination to careful scrutiny – doubly so when they converge in a country bordering Iran and allied with Israel. items.summary: Two supertankers hit mines near Hormuz, Iranian navy says Iran's navy said on Sunday that two supertankers hit naval mines and caught fire after entering a "restricted area" east of the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian media reported. According to the Fars news agency, the navy said the tankers had switched off their detection and navigation systems and struck the mines north of Ghanam Island. Both vessels reportedly stopped moving. Supertankers usually carry two million barrels of oil or more, about twice as much as a standard tanker. The navy also warned that relying on "smugglers such as CENTCOM", referring to US Central Command, would result in "nothing but heavy losses". UK Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) also said on Sunday it had received a report of an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman. It gave no further details, saying only that authorities were aware and an investigation was under way. It was unclear whether the incident involved either of the tankers Iran described. items.title: The best thing I ever ate? Lunch on the strait of Hormuz
items.summary: The idea of any guest being hungry, or there not being enough food, is an unspeakable proposition for an Iranian host When most people think of the strait of Hormuz, the warm, tropical waterway connecting the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman, incredible food isn’t usually the first thing that comes to mind. But it should be, and I would know – it’s where I had one of my most memorable meals. I was visiting Iran, traversing thousands of miles across the country with a local female photographer, mapping out regional specialities for my cookbook The Saffron Tales . Over the course of several months, we cooked and ate in people’s home kitchens, meeting a cross-section of society, from farmers and pharmacists to yoga teachers and restaurant owners, who all shared their favourite foods with us in places as diverse as the snowy mountains outside Tabriz, the rice paddies of the Caspian Sea, and the historic cities of Isfahan and Shiraz. Most vessels broadcasting AIS continued to use the Iranian route, although UKMTO noted an increase in traffic along the southern route. items.title: Trump envoys met Qatari officials in Berlin to discuss US-Iran mediation, report says
items.summary: Trump envoys met Qatari officials in Berlin to discuss US-Iran mediation, report says US President Donald Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met senior Qatari officials in Berlin on Thursday to discuss mediation efforts between the US and Iran , Axios reported on Friday, citing two sources with knowledge of the meeting. The meeting came as Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani was in Germany on a visit. Following talks with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Berlin, the emir called for diplomatic efforts to de-escalate conflicts across the Middle East. On the sidelines of the visit, Qatari Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani met his German counterpart Johann Wadephul. The two discussed ongoing diplomatic efforts and joint coordination to de-escalate tensions and enhance security and stability in the region, according to the Qatari foreign ministry.

items.title: Trump says US will find out about Iranian dirty bomb plot 'rumour'
items.summary: Trump says US will find out about Iranian dirty bomb plot 'rumour' US President Donald Trump said on Friday that there was a "rumour" that Iran was building a dirty bomb. He added that if Iran was doing so, the United States would find out and stop it. CNN had reported earlier this week that US intelligence indicated Iran could be attempting to build a dirty bomb and detonate it in Washington. Iran's foreign ministry denied the allegations on Tuesday, calling them "baseless". A dirty bomb is far less destructive than a nuclear bomb, which relies on a fission reaction. Speaking to reporters, Trump also repeated his claim that the US has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz. "Last week, we took out record amounts of oil from the Hormuz Strait. Our navy has a blockade," he said. "We have total control over the Hormuz Strait." "Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, ever," he added. US President Donald Trump points as reporters raise their hands to ask questions during a press conference at the White House in Washington, DC, 20 November 2026 (REUTERS/Kylie Cooper)

"The Iranians are after me. I'm not going to be cowered by the Iranians. Life on the military base is good," Bessent said in an interview with CNBC. The US Treasury has been tightening sanctions on Iran since the US and Israel launched strikes on the country in February. "Operation Economic Outcast, which we are two and a half months into, is the greatest economic isolation of any country in history," Bessent said. items.title: What Ukraine Hath Wrought: Lessons for War, If We’re Listening
items.summary: Four years into Russia’s war against Ukraine, what should the U.S. military have learned by now? Michael Kofman (Carnegie Endowment), Dara Massicot (Carnegie Endowment), and Amos Fox (Arizona State University) join Ryan to discuss. The easy answer is drones and AI, but our guests argue the harder truths lie elsewhere: “Old-fashioned” ideas like campaigning, holding territory, mass, and attrition still decide wars. And, as they discuss, based on U.S. performance in the war with Iran, it may be that not much learning has happened at all.Image: ArmyInform The post What Ukraine Hath Wrought: Lessons for War, If We’re Listening appeared first on War on the Rocks .

items.title: Tanker catches fire after projectile strike near Strait of Hormuz - UKMTO
items.summary: Tanker catches fire after projectile strike near Strait of Hormuz - UKMTO A tanker caught fire after a projectile struck it while sailing through the Strait of Hormuz, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency said on Friday. The incident occurred 8 nautical miles north of the Omani town of Khasab, UKMTO said, adding that no casualties or environmental impact were reported. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said shortly afterwards that an oil tanker had caught fire after hitting a mine while attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz near Khasab, Iranian media reported. Khasab is located on Oman's Musandam Peninsula at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: US must leave West Asia and return to its own region, Iranian lawmaker says
items.summary: US must leave West Asia and return to its own region, Iranian lawmaker says An Iranian lawmaker said the United States must withdraw from West Asia and return to its own geographic sphere. Major-General Mohammad Esmaeil Kowsari, a member of parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, told Iran’s Mehr news agency that the US could no longer confront Iran. He said Washington had issued shifting threats, at times discussing military action on the ground and at others threatening to open the Strait of Hormuz. Kowsari also pointed to US threats against Iran’s nuclear programme and proposals for an economic, land, air and naval blockade of the country. He said that Washington should leave West Asia and return to its own geographical sphere, which he said was 12,000km away.

items.title: Schumer doubles down on hawkery despite Van Hollen's anti-war test
items.summary: In some of his first remarks on the Senate floor since his leadership of the Democratic caucus was formally challenged, Sen. Chuck Schumer of New York blasted President Donald Trump for pursuing an insufficiently hawkish foreign policy. “Trump calls the trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin ‘historic’. Yes, it’s a historic embarrassment that people will remember long into the future,” Schumer said on Thursday. “It’s a betrayal of the United States.” Schumer went on to criticize the President for not securing any concessions from his counterparts, including on curbing Chinese espionage or preventing Beijing and Moscow from helping Iran target American troops. The emphasis of Schumer’s remarks was striking given that dissatisfaction with Trump’s foreign policy and its economic ramifications helped propel Democrats back into the Senate majority earlier this month. items.title: Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper hit in Houthi strike on Saudi wealth fund HQ
items.summary: By Timour Azhari RIYADH, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Riyadh's tallest skyscraper, headquarters of the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, was struck on Thursday by a suspected Houthi missile in the latest blow in the Iran-backed Yemeni group's war with the kingdom. The strike blew out windows across seven to eight floors of PIF Tower, bending parts of its metal facade. It was the second time in less than two weeks that a Houthi attack damaged a landmark in Riyadh's financial district, with state oil giant Aramco's building hit in a November 8 attack.

items.title: Trump says US will 'see what happens' in conflict with Iran after January 1
items.summary: Nov 19 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump said in comments broadcast on Thursday that the United States would "see what happens" in its conflict with Iran after January 1, without explaining what the significance of that date might be. In recent weeks, Trump has alternated between threats of escalation against Iran and indicating he could wind down hostilities, with the two sides in a standoff over efforts to resolve the conflict.

items.title: West presses Iran at IAEA to let inspections resume at bombed nuclear sites

Iran has not granted the International Atomic Energy Agency access to those nuclear facilities since the military strikes against them in June 2025.

items.title: Trump says he will 'see what happens' with Iran after 1 January
items.summary: Trump says he will 'see what happens' with Iran after 1 January US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that Washington would "see what happens" as regards its war on Iran after 1 January. “We're going to have a new year coming up, and we'll see what happens after January 1. But they've been nasty,” Trump told Fox News during his trip to China. Trump made the comments during an interview in which he was asked about a CNN report that Iran was planning to detonate a “dirty bomb” in Washington. A dirty bomb uses conventional explosives to spread radioactive material. Trump downplayed such a threat, saying “I don't think so”, when asked if people in the capital should be alarmed.

items.title: China issues 'peace declaration' agreed with Trump and Putin
items.summary: China issues 'peace declaration' agreed with Trump and Putin China has released a “peace declaration” it said its President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin had agreed on at their unprecedented three-way meeting, where they said nuclear wars were futile and should never be fought. All three countries committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security, according to a four-point declaration published by Chinese official media Xinhua. The leaders reportedly discussed Russia's war in Ukraine and the US-Israeli war on Iran. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons, Xinhua said. The three heads of state also agreed on reform for a "more effective" United Nations, and said that the International Criminal Court and similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction, according to the declaration.

"De energiesector en de wereldeconomie hebben dan wel weerbaarheid laten zien. Maar hoe langer de crisis duurt, hoe dieper deze zijn sporen nalaat. Het agentschap doet niet één toekomstvoorspelling, maar schetst verschillende scenario's van hoe de energiewereld zich zal ontwikkelen. items.title: APEC Summit: Lots of gloss, little real progress?
items.summary: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin are holding their first-ever trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC forum. It is a historic moment in more ways than one, with the leaders of the world’s three most powerful countries around the same table. Ukraine, the war in Iran, nuclear disarmament and artificial intelligence are all expected to be discussed, and the summit has stoked fears of a carve-up of the world into spheres of influence. But despite the buzz, analysts expect more symbolism than substance, with few concrete breakthroughs likely. Our correspondent in the region has more.

items.summary: Trump says US does not 'need any help' from China, Russia to end war on Iran US President Donald Trump said that Washington does not "need any help" from China or Russia to end the war on Iran. During an interview with Fox News, Trump said: "We don’t need any help. We’ve defeated their navy, we’ve defeated their air force, we’ve defeated their anti-aircraft." The comments come ahead of his expected  trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China. He also claimed that Tehran's missiles are "down to about 12, 13% of what they were, and they want to make a deal, so I don’t need help. I’m not going to go in asking for any help," adding that the US has "total control of the Hormuz Strait". "They want to make a deal, but I want a deal that can be lasting," the US president stressed. "I’m going to finish it off -- soon. I mean, one way or the other, we’ll finish it off."

It signed the Abraham Accords with Israel, and is also a deeply indebted nation, dependent on its wealthier neighbors for its survival. items.title: US sanctions Lebanese nationals, entities over Hezbollah links
items.summary: US sanctions Lebanese nationals, entities over Hezbollah links The US Treasury Department has imposed sanctions on three Lebanese individuals and three entities, which it accuses of aiding Hezbollah, in its latest effort to destroy the group’s financial networks around the world. In a statement, the department said it placed them on the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, without specifying the charges or the evidence against them. One of the organisations, "Wa Ta’awanu Association", was described as "a charity that provides cover for Hizballah’s activities under the guise of delivering humanitarian services". "The US government will continue to disrupt Iran’s attempts to exert influence in the region and fund its proxies," US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent added in a post on X. The Iranian regime’s attempts to infringe on Lebanon’s sovereignty through terror proxies like Hizballah will not be tolerated. items.title: Rubio says 'no imminent threat' to US from Iran
items.summary: Rubio says 'no imminent threat' to US from Iran US Secretary of State Marco Rubio cast doubt about reports of an "imminent threat" from Iran on Washington. Speaking to reporters in the Philippines, Rubio said that US authorities routinely check for  potential threats against the country, but added that most intelligence leads are not considered credible. When asked if he was concerned about a possible attack on Washington, he said: "I am not. But again, we're concerned every day about anything that threatens our country ... I don't think there's any imminent threat. "The United States is always on the lookout for anyone who tries to do harm to our country and to our people. items.title: Iran’s Ghalibaf warns US, Israel against targeting civilian infrastructure
items.summary: Iran’s Ghalibaf warns US, Israel against targeting civilian infrastructure Iran’s top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has warned of retaliation to the US and Israel after a New York Times report quoted analysts pointing to Tehran's "dual-use" of civilian infrastructure. "Prepping the next round on civilian infra, their 'experts' tell NYT: 'dams near Iran’s missile sites are dual-use.'," he mockingly referenced the article. "Cool. New rule: Any dam, port, or power plant near a US or Israeli base is dual-use. We’ll apply your logic consistently and even-handedly," Ghalibaf added. The US and Israel have previously attacked civilian areas and infrastructure across the region under the guise that they are used for military purpose, despite having no evidence for such claims. As a result, countless civilians have been killed and wounded in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.

items.title: Will Syria entry into Mecca pact mean clash with the Houthis?
items.summary: Syria appears likely to soon join the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, a collective defense agreement established several months ago by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan. This development would constitute a milestone in Damascus’ efforts to reassert itself within the region’s security architecture following Syria’s gruesome civil war. Membership in the pact could enhance the legitimacy and prestige of post-Assad Syria while bolstering its military capabilities and deepening partnerships with influential regional states. Syria could benefit from more intelligence cooperation, military training, and Saudi financial support. All this could complement Damascus’ existing security partnership with Ankara. But it’s not all milk and honey. Joining the security configuration could expose Syria to foreign conflicts and geopolitical rivalries while undermining Damascus’ ability to prioritize redevelopment at home. Woorden van die strekking liepen drie jaar geleden nog uit op een felle strijd, maar voorzitter Australië probeert het nu toch weer. Landen hebben vanaf nu de kans om te reageren op de tekst, waarmee eind deze week de klimaattop wordt afgesloten. De passages zouden dus nog aangepast of geschrapt kunnen worden. But let’s make an exception for Benjamin Netanyahu. Ever since his far-right coalition government lost its mandate in last month’s national elections, Israel’s prime minister has been making an ugly spectacle of himself. The Houthis have made rapid gains against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government sincethe US-Iran conflict reignited Yemen's frozen civil war this summer, drawing Riyadh back into confrontation with the group.

The government said last week that, though Iran has had gas shortages before, they would be more severe this winter because of war damage to processing plants and most regions would be affected.

items.title: Squabble over leadership risks plunging the OSCE into crisis
items.summary: The Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) is staring down the barrel of entering 2027 without a chair for the first time in its 51-year history. The Europeans are wrestling Turkey to drop its veto over Cyprus’ bid, raising the stakes by loudly opposing the only other candidate, Georgia. Unable to win over Ankara, Europe should drop its objections to Tbilisi to avert a crisis. With three weeks to go until the OSCE Ministerial Council in Lugano, Switzerland, on December 3, the organization remains deadlocked over who should lead it from 2027-28. The chairperson-in-office role rotates every two years and is normally voted on well in advance with agreement by consensus. EU member Cyprus was the first country to put its hat in the ring almost two years ago, in December 2024. However, Cyprus’ bid has been vetoed by Turkey on the basis of the long-standing dispute over the division of the island in 1974 . items.title: Trump's Africa envoy puts on a masterclass in bad diplomacy
items.summary: Since returning to the White House, President Donald Trump has increasingly relied on special envoys to deal with some of his most vexing foreign policy challenges. While Trump slashed the use of special envoys in his first term, he has come around in his second term, in part because they allow him to bypass his career foreign service officers by compartmentalizing information from “deep state bureaucrats” who he has accused of spying on him and leaking his dealmaking to the press. As in previous administrations, the current Trump administration has assembled a collection of envoys largely based on region and policy imperative. Regions like the Middle East, South and Central Asia, and the Arctic all have special envoys, as do specific countries like Syria, Belarus, Greenland, and Ukraine (currently vacant). Similarly high-profile or strategic policy objectives like hostage affairs and combating anti-Semitism also have designated special envoys. items.title: A Second Path Under the Caspian: What the Trans-Caspian Cable Changes for Eurasian Connectivity
items.summary: When the presidents of Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan inaugurated a 380-kilometer fiber-optic cable beneath the Caspian Sea on October 15, they opened the first fiber-optic link across the Caspian seabed. Designed for a capacity of at least 400 terabits per second, the cable matters chiefly because it creates an alternative: data moving between Central Asia and Europe can now take a westbound route that avoids Russian networks. Kazakhstan gains an additional international connection, and Azerbaijan strengthens its role as a transit hub. Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, which depend on Kazakhstan for international connectivity, stand to gain indirectly, and carriers and cloud providers gain another potential route between Asia and Europe. How far these gains extend will depend on how much traffic the link comes to carry.

items.summary: Nov 15 (Reuters) - Yemeni forces fighting for the internationally recognised Saudi-backed government said on Sunday that they were withdrawing from an area overlooking the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait, leaving the Iran-aligned Houthis in control. The government's retreat from the Bab el-Mandeb area hands the Houthis greater leverage over the maritime chokepoint, creating a potent pressure point on global shipping while Iran continues to disrupt traffic through the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula.

items.title: Yemeni government force retreats from strait in major setback in war against Houthis
items.summary: By Mohammed Ghobari Nov 15 (Reuters) - Yemeni government forces announced on Sunday they were withdrawing from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to focus on a defence of their main base in Aden, in a major setback for the Saudi-backed campaign against the Iran-aligned Houthis. The announcement signalled the apparent end of a six-week government counteroffensive to reclaim the coast near the mouth of the Red Sea, seized by the Houthis in September in a lightning advance that squeezed oil exports.

items.title: En Auschwitz con el heredero del Sah de Irán para apoyar a los judíos
items.summary: En fila india, en silencio y tiritando de frío, nuestras sombras avanzan por un túnel oscuro camino del matadero. A través de ese pasaje subterráneo en el que suenan los nombres de los judíos que aquí fueron exterminados, la visita al campo de concentración de Auschwitz sobrecoge desde la entrada, incluso antes de llegar a la puerta de hierro con su infame cartel 'El trabajo os hará libre' ('ARBEIT MACHT FREI', escrito en alemán en mayúsculas). Cuentan que la B de 'ARBEIT' ('trabajo') está al revés, más ancha por arriba que por abajo, porque así la puso un herrero polaco preso en el campo, Jan Liwacz, como pequeño gesto de rebeldía para demostrar la falsedad del eslogan: aquí nada traía la libertad, solo la muerte.Se calcula que en el campo de Auschwitz y en el de Birkenau, a tres kilómetros y medio, perecieron un millón de los seis millones de judíos que los nazis mataron en el Holocausto durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial (1939-45). The IRGC accused Israel of spreading misinformation. French authorities blame Shahid Kaveh for what they describe as the first large-scale cyber sabotage on French soil. On October 11 and 12, hackers drove temperatures inside refrigeration units to as high as 50C (122F) at about 700 stores. “Paris should beware the Zionist regime’s false flag trap,” IRGC spokesman Sardar Mohebi said on X. “Unlike the US and the Zionist regime, civilians have no place on the target list of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps,” he said, adding that the “ridiculous claim” is the “Zionists’ tired old playbook for stoking fear of Iran and winning allies in Europe”.

items.summary: Iran says three tankers hit by mines in Hormuz catch fire Iran's navy and Revolutionary Guards said on Saturday that fires had broken out on a total of three oil tankers that struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz. "A short while ago, two oil tankers that had switched off their radar and positioning systems and were secretly attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz through an unauthorised route exploded and caught fire after striking a naval mine," the Guards' navy said in a statement on the incident in the south of the waterway, carried by the Iranian state broadcaster early on Saturday. A separate statement from Iran's conventional navy said another tanker "navigating through the unsafe and prohibited zone east of the Strait of Hormuz with its tracking and identification systems switched off, caught fire and was forced to stop after striking a naval mine". The statements did not provide the names or origins of the vessels but the Guards said one of those hit in south Hormuz was a supertanker. items.title: Yalta became a byword for betrayal. Will Trump, Xi and Putin enact another carve-up?
items.summary: Russia and US approach potential summit seeking China’s help to extricate them from wars of choice, as Putin hopes to find consensus on new global order The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, is among those who have expressed concern that the world will witness a Yalta 2.0 moment if Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin meet trilaterally, as expected, on the sidelines of the Apec summit in China next week. It is a truism in diplomacy that if you are not around the table, the risk is that you, or your values, are on the menu and about to be carved up. Many excluded from the summit in Shenzhen, principally Ukraine but also eastern Europe and Baltic countries, Taiwan and even Iran, have reason to be nervous that their sponsors might abandon them in a complex geopolitical trade-off that Putin envisions, and Trump seems to endorse. items.title: 'What would be left of international legal order': Araghchi on US strikes
items.summary: 'What would be left of international legal order': Araghchi on US strikes "If states were free to attack one another based on their own assessments of possible future threats, what would be left of the international legal order?" Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has asked in an opinion piece for Japan's Kyodo News. "This question," Araghchi wrote, "goes well beyond the political dispute between Iran and the United States." "It concerns one of the fundamental principles on which the international order established after the Second World War rests: the use of force is governed by law, and no state, however powerful, is entitled to place its own judgment above binding rules of international law," the article read. He said the US-Israeli strikes constituted a clear violation of the prohibition on the use of force and an infringement of Iran's sovereignty. "Their legality must be assessed against the U.N. Dat werd vannacht door de Amerikaanse regering aan journalisten meegedeeld. De Chinese regering heeft het driepartijenoverleg niet bevestigd. Als dat overleg er komt, is het de eerste keer dat de leiders van die landen elkaar samen spreken. De ontmoeting zou plaatsvinden te midden van de Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) in de Chinese stad Shenzhen en zou onder meer gaan over het verminderen van kernwapens. "President Trump is van mening dat de uitbreiding van kernwapens zeer gevaarlijk is", zei woordvoerder Olivia Wales van het Witte Huis tegen verslaggevers. Het laatste kernwapenverdrag tussen de VS en Rusland liep in februari af. Anonieme analisten zeggen tegen de Amerikaanse pers dat ze geen nieuw akkoord verwachten. "Ik zou dit omschrijven als het startpunt, het eerste gesprek op het niveau van deze leiders tussen de landen", zegt een functionaris tegen CNN. items.title: Iran's navy claims US MQ-I drone shot down off southern coast
items.summary: Iran's navy claims US MQ-I drone shot down off southern coast Iranian navy has said it shot down a US MQ-1 drone near the coastal area of Kuhestak in the country’s southern Hormozgan Province, Iran's Islamic Republic News Agency (Irna) reported. The navy said in a statement the drone was intercepted and destroyed by its air defence system operating under the country’s integrated air defence network along the coast of Sirik, east of the Strait of Hormuz, according to Irna. The MQ-1 Predator is a medium-altitude, long-endurance remotely piloted aircraft developed by General Atomics and operated primarily by the US Air Force.

items.title: Trump extends shipping law waiver for 90 days amid Iran war fuel price rise
items.summary: Trump extends shipping law waiver for 90 days amid Iran war fuel price rise US President Donald Trump has extended by 90 days a waiver of a shipping law so that foreign-flagged ships can transport oil and other commodities between US ports, a White House official said on Friday. The administration would extend the waiver of the more than 100-year-old Jones Act, Reuters reported, citing industry sources. The administration issued a blanket waiver in March, a month after the US launched its war on Iran, in an effort to lower oil and fuel prices. When it extended the waiver in August, it said it would decide cases on a case-by-case basis, a condition that also applies to the latest extension. The Jones Act requires cargo moving between US ports to be carried on ships built in the US, owned by US companies, and crewed by American workers. The waiver aims to lower gasoline, diesel, and fertiliser prices, which have risen because of the war. items.title: US says it shot down two Iranian drones heading towards Bahrain
items.summary: US says it shot down two Iranian drones heading towards Bahrain The US military on Friday said it had shot down two Iranian attack drones launched towards Bahrain, denying an Iranian claim that its forces had struck a US early-warning radar system in the Gulf kingdom. US Central Command (Centcom) said the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launched two one-way attack drones towards Bahrain, both of which were intercepted by US forces. Centcom also rejected the IRGC’s claim that it had attacked a US early-warning radar in Bahrain earlier in the day. The competing accounts come amid questions from some US lawmakers about the Pentagon’s disclosure of details surrounding incidents in the conflict, while scepticism has also circulated on social media.

items.title: Belgian ministers at odds over Iran's alleged role in refrigerator cyberattacks
items.summary: BRUSSELS, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Belgian Interior Minister Bernard Quintin said Iran was "very likely" behind the recent refrigerator cyberattacks on European shops, while Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot said there was insufficient evidence to draw conclusions. "There was enough evidence from our security services for me to say that Iran is very likely behind the cyberattacks we have seen targeting our shops," Quintin told Belgian broadcaster VRT NWS Thursday evening. Quintin made similar comments earlier on Thursday, but Prévot struck a more cautious tone.

items.title: Iran reports shooting down US Predator drone off its southern coast
items.summary: Iran reports shooting down US Predator drone off its southern coast Iran’s navy said on Friday that it shot down a US MQ-1 Predator drone over the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian media. The semi-official IRNA news agency reported that the drone was downed near the Sirik coast in the Kuhestak region. The navy said it “will not hesitate for a moment” to defend Iran’s territorial integrity, maritime borders and interests. Images shared by IRNA appear to show damaged components of military hardware.

items.title: IAEA increasingly concerned about Iranian enrichment plant, its report says
items.summary: VIENNA, Nov 13 (Reuters) - The UN nuclear watchdog is "increasingly concerned" about a uranium-enrichment plant at Isfahan that Iran declared to it last year but has still not let the watchdog inspect, it said in a confidential report on Iran on Friday seen by Reuters. Iran has not let International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors return to any of its nuclear facilities bombed by Israel and the United States in a 12-day campaign in June last year that destroyed or badly damaged Iran's other uranium enrichment plants, the heart of its nuclear programme.
